section: A. What burnout is and is not
citation: World Health Organization. (2019). Burn-out an "occupational phenomenon": International Classification of Diseases.
scope_limitation: Definition only; not a diagnostic instrument; limited to the occupational context.

section: A. What burnout is and is not
citation: Maslach, C., & Leiter, M. P. (2016). Understanding the burnout experience: Recent research and its implications for psychiatry. World Psychiatry, 15(2), 103–111.
scope_limitation: Cross-occupational; written by the model's originators; no teacher-specific effect sizes.

section: A. What burnout is and is not
citation: Bianchi, R., Schonfeld, I. S., & Laurent, E. (2015). Burnout–depression overlap: A review. Clinical Psychology Review, 36, 28–41.
scope_limitation: Authors argue a contested position; shows the boundary is unclear, not that burnout equals depression.

section: B. Demands control and helplessness
citation: Karasek, R. A. (1979). Job demands, job decision latitude, and mental strain: Implications for job redesign. Administrative Science Quarterly, 24(2), 285–308.
scope_limitation: 1970s Swedish and American worker surveys; not teachers.

section: B. Demands control and helplessness
citation: Bakker, A. B., Demerouti, E., & Sanz-Vergel, A. (2023). Job demands–resources theory: Ten years later. Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior, 10, 25–53.
scope_limitation: General model across occupations; teacher tests are in Section C.

section: B. Demands control and helplessness
citation: Maier, S. F., & Seligman, M. E. P. (2016). Learned helplessness at fifty: Insights from neuroscience. Psychological Review, 123(4), 349–367.
scope_limitation: Mechanistic evidence mainly from animal and laboratory studies; a frame, not an occupational finding.

section: C. What drives burnout in teaching
citation: Aloe, A. M., Shisler, S. M., Norris, B. D., Nickerson, A. B., & Rinker, T. W. (2014). A multivariate meta-analysis of student misbehavior and teacher burnout. Educational Research Review, 12, 30–44.
scope_limitation: Correlational and mostly cross-sectional; direction of effect not established.

section: C. What drives burnout in teaching
citation: Collie, R. J., Shapka, J. D., & Perry, N. E. (2012). School climate and social–emotional learning: Predicting teacher stress, job satisfaction, and teaching efficacy. Journal of Educational Psychology, 104(4), 1189–1204.
scope_limitation: Cross-sectional self-report; Canadian sample.

section: C. What drives burnout in teaching
citation: Hakanen, J. J., Bakker, A. B., & Schaufeli, W. B. (2006). Burnout and work engagement among teachers. Journal of School Psychology, 43(6), 495–513.
scope_limitation: Cross-sectional; Finnish sample; broad demand and resource measures.

section: C. What drives burnout in teaching
citation: Skaalvik, E. M., & Skaalvik, S. (2014). Teacher self-efficacy and perceived autonomy: Relations with teacher engagement, job satisfaction, and emotional exhaustion. Psychological Reports, 114(1), 68–77.
scope_limitation: Cross-sectional; Norwegian sample; autonomy is self-reported perception.

section: C. What drives burnout in teaching
citation: Skaalvik, E. M., & Skaalvik, S. (2021). Teacher burnout: Relations between dimensions of burnout, perceived school context, job satisfaction and motivation for teaching. A longitudinal study. Teachers and Teaching, 27(7), 602–616.
scope_limitation: Two time points in one school year; Norwegian high school teachers; not experimental.

section: C. What drives burnout in teaching
citation: Madigan, D. J., & Kim, L. E. (2021). Towards an understanding of teacher attrition: A meta-analysis of burnout, job satisfaction, and teachers' intentions to quit. Teaching and Teacher Education, 105, 103425.
scope_limitation: Intentions to quit, not actual attrition; time-trend finding should be read cautiously.

section: C. What drives burnout in teaching
citation: Steiner, E. D., Levine, P. R., & Doan, S. (2026). Teacher well-being, pay, and intentions to leave in 2026: Selected findings from the 2026 State of the American Teacher survey. RAND Corporation, RR-A4404-2.
scope_limitation: Descriptive prevalence; funded by NEA and AFT (disclosed); technical report RR-A4404-3 holds full tables.

section: D. Mistreatment and institutional response
citation: McMahon, S. D., Reaves, S., McConnell, E. A., Peist, E., Ruiz, L., & APA Task Force on Classroom Violence Directed Against Teachers. (2017). The ecology of teachers' experiences with violence and lack of administrative support. American Journal of Community Psychology, 60(3–4), 502–515.
scope_limitation: Self-selected accounts of unsupportive responses; documents the experience, not its prevalence; teacher perspective only.

section: D. Mistreatment and institutional response
citation: McMahon, S. D., Worrell, F. C., Reddy, L. A., Martinez, A., Espelage, D. L., Astor, R. A., Anderman, E. M., Valido, A., Swenski, T., Perry, A. H., Dudek, C. M., & Bare, K. (2024). Violence and aggression against educators and school personnel, retention, stress, and training needs: National survey results. American Psychologist.
scope_limitation: Convenience sample; likely over-represents those who experienced violence; cross-sectional.

section: D. Mistreatment and institutional response
citation: Smith, C. P., & Freyd, J. J. (2014). Institutional betrayal. American Psychologist, 69(6), 575–587.
scope_limitation: Developed in sexual-assault and military contexts; application to schools is by analogy.

section: E. Moral distress demoralization and moral injury
citation: Morley, G., Ives, J., Bradbury-Jones, C., & Irvine, F. (2019). What is "moral distress"? A narrative synthesis of the literature. Nursing Ethics, 26(3), 646–662.
type: Systematic review and narrative synthesis (34 papers)
scope_limitation: Nursing and health-care ethics only; not tested in teaching.

section: E. Moral distress demoralization and moral injury
citation: Litz, B. T., Stein, N., Delaney, E., Lebowitz, L., Nash, W. P., Silva, C., & Maguen, S. (2009). Moral injury and moral repair in war veterans: A preliminary model and intervention strategy. Clinical Psychology Review, 29(8), 695–706.
scope_limitation: Built for combat veterans; included to distinguish the term, not to apply it to educators.

section: E. Moral distress demoralization and moral injury
citation: Santoro, D. A. (2018). Demoralized: Why teachers leave the profession they love and how they can stay. Harvard Education Press.
scope_limitation: Small self-selected sample of experienced teachers who stayed; conceptual distinction from burnout not psychometrically tested.

section: F. What helps
citation: Iancu, A. E., Rusu, A., Măroiu, C., Păcurar, R., & Maricuțoiu, L. P. (2018). The effectiveness of interventions aimed at reducing teacher burnout: A meta-analysis. Educational Psychology Review, 30, 373–396.
scope_limitation: Nearly all interventions were individual-directed; cannot compare with organizational change.

section: F. What helps
citation: Panagioti, M., Panagopoulou, E., Bower, P., Lewith, G., Kontopantelis, E., Chew-Graham, C., Dawson, S., van Marwijk, H., Geraghty, K., & Esmail, A. (2017). Controlled interventions to reduce burnout in physicians: A systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA Internal Medicine, 177(2), 195–205.
scope_limitation: Physicians, not teachers; organizational-versus-individual finding not replicated in schools.
